title: Cross-platform capability and platform-service vocabulary
description: Shared finite vocabularies and bounded supporting records for the M01-W07 platform-service boundary. Enum tokens use the repository UPPER_SNAKE_CASE grammar; MACOS_ARM64, WINDOWS_X64, and UBUNTU_X64 are the exact specification targets macos-arm64, windows-x64, and ubuntu-x64. Nothing here certifies a platform, resolves a path, opens a secret store, spawns a process, registers a native host, locates a browser, runs a model, installs, or updates. Version 1.1.0 adds STORE_AVAILABLE so a successful STATUS availability probe is structurally representable.

platformId.title: Detected platform target identifier
platformId.description: Closed target vocabulary. UNSUPPORTED_TARGET is a recognized but uncertified target; UNKNOWN_TARGET is an unrecognized or unevaluated target. Neither may ever carry a certified support tier.

certifiedPlatformId.title: Certified first-release target identifier
certifiedPlatformId.description: The exact three certified first-release targets. Windows 10, Intel macOS, Windows ARM64, and non-Ubuntu Linux distributions are deliberately absent.

supportTier.title: Platform support tier
supportTier.description: CERTIFIED_FULL is complete core plus an accepted local-AI profile; CERTIFIED_CORE is deterministic core workflows with AI unavailable or below the performance tier; EXPERIMENTAL carries no support promise; UNSUPPORTED is blocked with an explanation. A support tier is a reviewed claim, never a self-asserted request field.

platformCapabilityId.title: Platform capability family
platformCapabilityId.description: Closed set of specification-owned platform capability families reported by the platform service.

capabilityAvailability.title: Capability availability state
capabilityAvailability.description: AVAILABLE and DEGRADED_LIMITED are the only non-blocking states. NOT_EVALUATED and UNKNOWN are explicitly not success. UNSUPPORTED_TARGET means the capability cannot exist on this target at all.

platformReasonCode.title: Finite platform reason code
platformReasonCode.description: Closed, user-safe, redaction-safe reason vocabulary. Reason codes never carry host paths, registry values, device identifiers, machine secrets, or free-form operating-system text.

platformComponentId.title: Platform component identifier
platformComponentId.description: The typed platform interfaces defined by specification §5.14.2. Shared domain code addresses these components instead of operating-system APIs.

evaluationMethod.title: How a platform observation was produced
evaluationMethod.description: NOT_EVALUATED and DECLARED_PLAN are never measured evidence. Only MEASURED_NATIVE_RUN represents execution on the actual operating-system family and architecture.

installationScope.title: Installation scope
installationScope.description: Per-user is the preferred default; SYSTEM scope is a reviewed exception, never a caller-chosen escalation.

pathRole.title: Typed logical path role
pathRole.description: The complete caller-facing path vocabulary. A caller selects a role; it can never supply an absolute path, traversal path, UNC or device path, registry path, shell or environment expansion, executable lookup input, or arbitrary working directory.

pathSegment.title: Bounded relative path segment
pathSegment.description: One already-normalized relative segment. Separators, traversal, drive letters, device prefixes, home shorthand, and environment expansion cannot be expressed.

redactedPathReference.title: Sanitized logical path reference
redactedPathReference.description: A trusted adapter result may report a resolved location only in sanitized form: an angle-bracketed role placeholder followed by bounded normalized relative segments. Absolute paths, drive letters, UNC and device prefixes, backslashes, traversal, home-directory shorthand, environment expansion, and registry syntax are structurally unrepresentable.

productVersion.title: Bounded product version
productVersion.description: One to four dot-separated non-negative components without leading zeros. Covers semantic versions and four-component browser/runtime versions.

buildToken.title: Bounded operating-system build token
buildToken.description: Opaque vendor build label. It cannot carry whitespace, path separators, shell syntax, or machine identity.

browserFamily.title: Browser family
browserFamily.description: Chrome stable is the only certified browser. UNKNOWN_BROWSER records a recognized-but-uncertified observation and can never be certified.

browserChannel.title: Browser release channel
browserChannel.description: Only STABLE is certified. UNKNOWN_CHANNEL is an honest unevaluated observation.

extensionId.title: Chrome extension identifier
extensionId.description: Exactly 32 characters from the Chrome extension alphabet. Only allowlisted identifiers may appear in a registration contract.

nativeHostName.title: Native-messaging host name
nativeHostName.description: Chrome native-messaging host name grammar: lowercase alphanumeric and underscore segments separated by dots. It is an identity, never a filesystem path or executable name.

secretKeyRole.title: Bounded secret key role
secretKeyRole.description: Closed set of reviewed secret roles owned by the local product. An untrusted caller cannot name a keychain service/account, a Windows registry location, or a D-Bus request. External-provider tokens are deliberately absent and remain future work.

secretReference.title: Opaque secret reference
secretReference.description: Bounded opaque handle for secret material held by the platform store. It is never the secret itself and never appears in diagnostics or evidence with a value attached.

secretOperation.title: Secret-store operation
secretOperation.description: STATUS is an availability probe that never touches secret material.

secretResultState.title: Secret-store result state
secretResultState.description: Result states never carry secret bytes. RETRIEVED reports only that material exists behind an opaque reference. STORE_AVAILABLE is the successful STATUS availability probe; it never accompanies material.

processProfileId.title: Approved process profile
processProfileId.description: Closed set of reviewed executable profiles. A spawn plan names a profile; it can never carry an executable path, executable name, interpreter, or command text.

environmentVariableId.title: Allowlisted environment variable
environmentVariableId.description: Closed set of reviewed variable identifiers. An arbitrary environment dictionary is structurally unrepresentable, and no allowlisted variable may carry credential material.

value.description: Bounded inert token. Whitespace, shell metacharacters, markup, and path separators are excluded by the token grammar.

processArgument.title: Bounded process argument
processArgument.description: One already-separated argument. Arguments are never concatenated into a command line and never interpreted by a shell.

stdioMode.title: Process stdio mode
stdioMode.description: BINARY_LENGTH_PREFIXED is the Windows-safe native-messaging mode. Raw file-descriptor numbers are structurally unrepresentable.

processState.title: Process lifecycle state
processState.description: UNAVAILABLE means the supervisor itself could not observe the process. ORPHANED means the child outlived its supervising parent and requires cleanup.

terminationRequest.title: Typed termination request
terminationRequest.description: Typed intent only. Raw signal numbers, signal names, and platform-specific kill semantics are deliberately not representable.

distributionChannel.title: Packaging and update channel
distributionChannel.description: NOT_CONFIGURED is the honest state while no signed channel exists. TEST_SYNTHETIC is never a release claim.

userDataPreservation.title: User-data preservation indicator
userDataPreservation.description: EXPLICIT_DELETION_REQUESTED is the only state in which user data may be removed, and it requires an explicit user request recorded elsewhere.

runtimeFamily.title: Local model runtime family
runtimeFamily.description: Closed runtime vocabulary for the accepted local Ollama paths. External providers are deliberately absent and remain non-core future work.

profileAcceptanceState.title: Model-runtime profile acceptance state
profileAcceptanceState.description: ACCEPTED requires artifact and runtime evidence and a certified target. No Windows or Ubuntu profile is accepted today.

coreCapabilityBehavior.title: Deterministic-core behavior when AI is limited
coreCapabilityBehavior.description: Deterministic core workflows must remain usable in every state. FULL_AI_AVAILABLE additionally requires an accepted profile.

diagnosticResult.title: Diagnostic outcome
diagnosticResult.description: SUCCESS may not coexist with a blocking reason. BLOCKED means an external boundary prevented evaluation.

machineClass.title: Evidence machine class
machineClass.description: Coarse machine class only. Hostnames, serial numbers, user names, MAC addresses, and other machine-specific identity are never represented.

evidenceArtifactKind.title: Cross-platform evidence artifact kind
evidenceArtifactKind.description: Every artifact reference is a digest of a synthetic-safe artifact. Raw logs, environment dumps, registry exports, and machine PII are never embedded.

capabilityState.title: Capability state record
capabilityState.description: One capability observation. Availability, the evidence method, and the finite reason list are always explicit; an unevaluated capability is never reported as success.

reason_codes.description: Finite reasons explaining a non-available state. An AVAILABLE capability carries none.

identity_token.description: Bounded identity of the concrete provider observed (for example a secret-store backend family). Required evidence for an AVAILABLE capability.

detected_version.description: Observed provider version. Required evidence for an AVAILABLE capability.

supportClaim.title: Reviewed support claim
supportClaim.description: Separates a claimed tier from the reviewed tier and its evidence. A claim is inert data; only the reviewed tier plus evaluated-revision and evidence references may be treated as certification.

claimed_tier.description: Tier proposed by the producing adapter or record. Untrusted.

reviewed_tier.description: Tier accepted after independent review. UNSUPPORTED until proven.

requestContext.title: Platform request context
requestContext.description: Trusted routing metadata attached to every caller-facing platform request. The requesting principal is authenticated elsewhere; content scripts, model runtimes, and the public index can never be valid platform requesters.

artifactIdentity.title: Bounded artifact identity
artifactIdentity.description: Names a package or model artifact by identity and digest only. No download URL, mirror, signing key, or filesystem location is representable.

processExitCode.title: Bounded process exit code
processExitCode.description: Unsigned exit status covering POSIX and Windows ranges. Raw signal values are deliberately absent.

contextTokens.title: Bounded model context window in tokens

boundedUserMessage.title: Bounded user-safe message
boundedUserMessage.description: Short remediation text intended for a human. The character set excludes markup, path separators, shell syntax, and interpolation.
